reviews.author: Andi Shyti
reviews.summary: Approved the patch with a Reviewed-by tag, indicating that it meets kernel coding standards.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Dmitry,

On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 08:19:46AM +0000, Dmitry Ilvokhin wrote:
> Commit 22302af28d3f ("cleanup: Annotate guard constructors with
> nonnull") added the macro __nonnull_args() to wrap raw compiler
> attribute.
> 
> Replace __attribute__((nonnull)) with __nonnull_args() to standardize
> nonnull attribute usage across the tree and keep the attribute's quirks
> in one place rather than open-coded at every call site.
> 
> Suggested-by: Miguel Ojeda <miguel.ojeda.sandonis@gmail.com>
> Signed-off-by: Dmitry Ilvokhin <d@ilvokhin.com>

Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@linux.intel.com>

Thanks,
Andi

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch series aims to standardize the use of non-null attributes across the kernel by replacing raw compiler attributes with the __nonnull_args() macro. The first patch in the series, [PATCH 07/10], specifically targets the drm/gem module and replaces __attribute__((nonnull)) with __nonnull_args(). This change is intended to keep attribute quirks in one place rather than having them scattered throughout the code.

reviews.author: Miguel Ojeda
reviews.summary: Clarified that the drm/gem module should not include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> explicitly, as it is handled by the build machinery.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32 AM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
>
> Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?

No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
custom with the compiler flags etc.).

I hope that helps!

Cheers,
Miguel

reviews.author: Andy Shevchenko
reviews.summary: Initially suggested that the patch might be unnecessary, but later retracted this comment and suggested cleaning up headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> >
> > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> 
> No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> custom with the compiler flags etc.).

Usually it comes to the mere drivers via types.h, in rare cases (usually some
more generic library headers, we do better granularity as it affects the almost
entire kernel. Just double check that types.h is explicitly included.

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko

reviews.author: Andy Shevchenko
reviews.summary: Told the patch author to discard his previous comment, and suggested cleaning up headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 01:12:06PM +0000, Dmitry Ilvokhin wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> > On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> > >
> > > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> > 
> > No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> > custom with the compiler flags etc.).
> 
> Just to add a bit more colour to Miguel's reply.
> 
> I believe idea behind include/linux/compiler_attributes.h is to make
> attribute wrappers as simple and transparent to use as native compiler
> attributes. In particular, this means they should be available in every
> kernel compilation unit without any additional effort.
> 
> For this reason, all the nessesary plumbing is handled at the build
> machinery level (see scripts/Makefile.lib:171), where '-include'
> compiler flag is used to pull in include/linux/compiler_types.h, which
> in turn pulls include/linux/compiler_attributes.h.

Ah, TIL! Please, discard my comment then. Perhaps we need to clean up all
headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly (the same way
we do for kconfig.h).

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko
